title: Kosa Pan's Siamese embassy to Louis XIV, 1686
summary: King Narai of Siam sent Kosa Pan, with two other ambassadors and the Jesuit Guy Tachard, on two French ships back to France with a proposal for an eternal alliance. They landed at Brest and went to Versailles, where on 1 September 1686 they gave Narai's letter to Louis XIV; they stayed in France from June 1686 to March 1687. Thai ikat inspired French siamoise cloth, and Le Brun painted Kosa Pan. The sea road is drawn by the usual way round the Cape; the article gives no ports. The way home is not drawn, for the article gives none.

events.label: Narai's letter given to Louis XIV at Versailles
events.text: The ambassadors bowed to the king and gave him King Narai's letter, proposing an eternal alliance; he then showed them the royal apartments and gardens.
